    Urbanisation¶

    Given the substantial variation in light emissions both across and within continents, and the fact that most conflicts occur in economically less developed regions, it is crucial to understand where NTL can provide a reliable baseline. Building on the findings of Bara and Sticher, who show that establishing a minimum light baseline is not feasible in much of the Global South, this study seeks to identify the level of urbanisation required for NTL to serve as a meaningful baseline for conflict monitoring.

    For this purpose, we use the Degree of Urbanisation product (GHS‑SMOD V2‑0) from the GHSL, which provides a global rural–urban classification at 1 km resolution. The dataset combines built-up surface (GHS‑BUILT‑S R2023A) and population (GHS‑POP R2023A) data to assign each grid cell to one of nine settlement classes: water, very low-density rural, low-density rural, rural cluster, suburban or peri‑urban, semi‑dense urban cluster, dense urban cluster, and urban centre. In this study, we restrict the analysis to the 2020 layer.

    We first resample the Black Marble monthly composite data to match the GHS‑SMOD resolution. For each pixel, we then derive a binary NTL indicator (lit or unlit), its corresponding level of urbanisation, and its geographic location. This enables a directly comparable analysis of Europe and Africa at equivalent levels of urbanisation. Subsequently, we analyse the continuous radiance values across continents and, finally, examine the relationship between country-level mean radiance and the Human Development Index.

    dfs = []

for continent in CONTINENTS:
    df = pd.read_parquet(
        "results/urbanization_sept",
        filters=[("continent", "==",  continent)],
    )
    df = df[(~df.smod_code.isin([-200, 10])) & (df.black_marble_radiance_monthly >= 0)]
    high = df.black_marble_radiance_monthly.quantile(0.999)
    df = df[df.black_marble_radiance_monthly < high]
    df["bm_binary"] = df.black_marble_radiance_monthly > 1
    df["smod_class"] = df["smod_code"].map(SMOD_CODE_MAPPING)
    df["smod_class"] = pd.Categorical(
        df["smod_class"],
        categories=SMOD_CLASS_ORDER,
        ordered=True
    )

    df["country_name"] = df["country_code"].apply(
        lambda x: pycountry.countries.get(alpha_3=x).name
        if pycountry.countries.get(alpha_3=x)
        else "Invalid Code"
    )

    dfs.append(df)

df = pd.concat(dfs)
df.continent = df.continent.cat.remove_unused_categories()

    Radiance by Urbanisation Level¶

    We compared the average radiance and binary values across SMOD classes and continents. As shown below, most pixels in Europe – up to the rural cluster class – exhibit radiance values above 1 $\text{nW}/\text{cm}^{-2}/\text{sr}^{-1}$. In contrast, in Africa, this pattern holds only for urban centers. Notably, even in African built-up areas only around 60% of pixels are lit, which is similar to the illumination levels observed in rural clusters in Europe. Considering that many conflicts occur in poorer and more rural regions, the radiance values in these areas are often too low to reliably separate meaningful signals from background noise.

    We then examined the mean radiance values by SMOD class and country to assess how development differences among countries within each continent compare. As shown below, the spread of mean radiance values in Europe is considerably larger than in Africa. More interestingly, the correlations between HDI and mean monthly radiance values in Europe are weak – a pattern consistent across all SMOD classes. In Africa, however, particularly in more urban regions, radiance values exhibit a stronger positive correlation with development level.

    import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

with sns.axes_style("whitegrid", {"grid.color": ".9", "grid.linestyle": ":"}):

    plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))
    ax = sns.stripplot(
        data=corr_df,
        x="corr_hdi_black_marble",
        y="smod_class",
        hue="continent",
        orient="h",
        size=10,
        jitter=False,
        palette=PALETTE,
        linewidth=1,
        edgecolor="w"
    )

    ax.set(
        xlim=(0, 1),
        xlabel="Correlation (HDI vs mean radiance of Black Marble)",
        ylabel=""
    )

    ax.xaxis.grid(False)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True)
    sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)

    # Legend on top, horizontal, 2 columns
    handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
    ax.legend(
        handles=handles,
        labels=labels,
        title="Continent",
        loc="upper center",
        bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.12),
        ncol=2,
        frameon=False
    )

    plt.tight_layout()
